To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of random instances in a known motif significantly affects the power of detection of the motif and that the power of detection is a non-monotonic increasing function of the length of the motif, and that the length of the sequence affects the power of motif detection in a non-monotonical manner.
the presence of a known motif in the background sequence affects the power of detection for patterns within the motif and the power of detection can be calculated using efficient algorithms.
the power of detecting enriched patterns is a function of the number of random instances of known motif, the length of the sequence and the pattern of interest.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how the known occurrence of random instances of motifs affects the power of detection of enriched patterns.
developing a theoretical framework for the power analysis of detecting enriched patterns.
the power of detection of patterns in a set of sequences of unknown length.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of a known motif in a sequence affects the power of detection of patterns within the motif and the power is a function of the length and the number of instances of the known motif in the sequence.
the power of detecting a motif pattern in a set of sequences is affected by the presence of the known motif in the sequence.
the presence of a motif in a sequence affects the detection of a pattern within the motif, the extent of the effect depending on the pattern length and the number of occurrences of the motif.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the known presence of instances of a known TF motif in a sequence of interest increases the power of detecting enriched patterns.
the known presence of a motif in a sequence has a significant effect on the power of detection of patterns.
the presence of random instances in a long sequence of a known motif does affect the power of detection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of random instances can greatly affect the power of detecting enriched patterns.
the presence of a known motif in a sequence has a profound effect on the power of detection of patterns within the motif.
the power of detecting a pattern is affected by the length of the motif, the frequency of random occurrences of the motif, and the frequency of the pattern.
